contract: Supervised host for the assembly/run-engine Runs of one node, for text model calls of integration/ai-text: start_link takes owner_id (1..200 bytes), max_runs (a reservation table from start_run/3 or wake/2 through confirmed teardown; the host's own Registries and dedicated Unit DynamicSupervisor with max_children max_runs for one DynamicUnits directory with idle_ms), Unit, Run, evidence, EffectIntent journal and activation Store views of one namespace whose writes are compare-and-set on their stream heads, one Lease over the Run view (clock :store on PostgreSQL, one manual-clock backend on Memory), the engine clock, lease_ttl_ms (1..86,400,000) and the spec callback, and optionally fencing_proof, on_terminal, on_lost, allow_volatile and name; an exit of its infrastructure stops the host with that reason after it stops every Run. A spec holds the stable Run, operation and first Attempt IDs, a unit of 1..155 bytes (streams unit/<unit>, run/<unit> as the lease key, evidence/<unit>), provider_refs, tenant, principal, pattern, schemas, its finish, ask_person and nested_callable bindings (any other kind is refused at start as outside_profile), the AI binding descriptors, gate, context, Budget, budget_rule, request cap, Run deadline and the result reader's retention. start_run/3 reserves, claims the lease key, provisions the EffectIntent startup bindings once, starts the Run owner, creates the Run and begins the spec's Attempt (a retry gets {:unchanged, :duplicate, _} and begins none), and starts the evidence Writer, AsyncWork, a per-Run keep-alive and the engine with result_reader; a lease another owner holds is {:error, {:lease_refused, refusal}} with no engine. input/5, control/5, status/2, deadlines/2, result/4 and transcript/4 pass through ({:error, :not_running} for a Run not live on this host); each input and control is admitted by a sample of the lease clock against the until of its own admission snapshot ({:error, :lease_lost}, or {:error, :unavailable} with no reading; a reading older than a confirmed renewal is admitted again); control/5 forwards every control but Approval; after a terminal outcome input/5 and control/5 give {:error, :terminal} (also one queued before the worker read the outcome, with no engine call: after any engine start, input or control a caller's input or control is forwarded only once a read of the Run after it has succeeded, {:error, :unavailable} while that read fails, and the host's own inputs wait only for the read after a control) and on_terminal is called; reap/2 stops and confirms every per-Run process (by the Run's group leader, tasks and EffectIntent owners included, the callbacks it runs as Run tasks and the group leader itself, after every host task of the Run has exited: the host applies a task's result when it arrives, and frees the slot or hands the key to a next tenure only after the task's exit, a release's too; each lease reader is stopped and awaited by its task, at its deadline at the latest, also after it replied), then releases the lease and frees the slot with no attestation, or gives {:error, :release_unconfirmed} and keeps it; a failed start whose release is unconfirmed keeps the slot and retries the release, whoever joined its wait, and a start or wake of the Run, also one waiting on the release, takes the key over and owes the old lease's release until its own claim succeeds, the key reserved by that tenure meanwhile (another Run of the same Unit is identity_in_use, also while the tenure's spec callback runs). AI bindings: the idempotency key is the SHA-256 of {run_id, attempt_id, action_id} with the Attempt the engine committed for the action (after a control nothing is forwarded until the current Attempt is read again); an ai-text admission refusal is a gate denial recorded before any intent (no intent, no provider call); facts/1 repeats the passed admission with no I/O; every sink delivery goes to the Run's worker, which routes it by the committed model_call actions of the transcript and the binding configuration (the deliveries of a Run held until that Run's route is verified at a start or wake; the worker announces the Run started to the host before it submits a held delivery, so a terminal outcome reaches a live Run and calls on_terminal; start_run/3 and wake/2 answer once every Run of the call has finished route verification, and that answer and the submission of held deliveries have no order between them (in a batch a verified Run can submit them, and even end, while another still verifies); kept across a failed read; a route that cannot be read failing a start or wake as {:route, reason}; each held delivery handled by its kind) into one action_outcome input under an ID of Run, the action's Attempt and occurrence, whose frame and whole context (a future pause_deadline from the trusted context under budget_rule :pause, taken again only after the engine refused a passed one before appending) the first submission fixes for every retry; an acknowledged input is never submitted again; completed is completed/dispatched with the descriptor's usage conversion as actual (none without reported usage), a completed view over the engine's payload bound (65,536 bytes of compact JSON or 32 levels) is refused too_large dispatched with no actual, so its reservation stays reserved, refused is not_dispatched with actual 0 only for credentials_unavailable and input_unavailable and dispatched otherwise, unknown is unknown dispatch with no actual except malformed_response (dispatched), each under elzoo.ai-text.result v1 in the README's completed or refusal view; sink_failed gives no input and is reported; the keep-alive, independent of the worker, keeps the Unit awake from each engine start, input or control until a status read shows no model call ready or running, and an idle Run sleeps. wake/2 gives one disposition per Run (:woken or a README reason), opens only Runs with a current Attempt, rebuilds the spec (another fingerprint is incompatible_recovery with the Unit stopped and confirmed), and before any engine on an existing Run or Unit journal (wake/2, or a start_run/3 retry that opens one) requires a fresh :fenced from fencing_proof, asked at each check: no predecessor process can still act and no Store write that a predecessor submitted can still commit, on this node or another (the host's own confirmed teardown is no proof; with no fencing_proof every check fails), else fencing_unproven with no engine and no activation granted; a fresh start needs no check; an activation is granted only while the callback's lease reading shows this owner's lease active, before both its own until and the last confirmed one. One wake timer per Run from deadlines/1 (while paused the earlier of the Run and pause deadlines), refreshed after each start, wake, input and control and never fired on a failed read, sends one wake under a digest ID of Run, current Attempt and deadline; a replaced timer sends none, and a wake the engine did not take is sent again only by its timer, at least a second later, after the deadline and Attempt are read again. The Run's deadline is the node time by which the earlier of the last confirmed until (the claim's, then each confirmed renewal's) and the until of the newest live reading of the lease passes, taken from that reading's lease-clock sample; readings are ordered by the Store's head revision, then the lease-clock sample, never by their arrival at the host, so a confirmation that arrives late never restores a longer deadline that a newer reading shortened, and a newer reading that arrives after a confirmation still shortens it. Lease renewal through RunApprovalRelease.renew/2 half the TTL before the deadline, once per confirmed until and only while the newest reading shows the lease record that the host confirmed; a renewal that replied is confirmed by a live reading taken after its reply (its own, or, when that brings none, one that the host takes until the current deadline); an expiry check min(200 ms, TTL/4) before the deadline, whose live reading moves the deadline; at the deadline, unless moved, the Run is lost :expired with no reading; every lease reading of a renewal or an expiry check runs in a reader given up at the deadline at which it started; a lease_lost, fenced, indeterminate or unknown result, a renewal that exits, a reading at or past the last confirmed until, no confirmed renewal by the deadline (the node's clock never stands in for a reading), or a reading with another holder or none stops admission ({:error, :lease_lost}), fences the Run's processes and calls on_lost once, when that result arrives and for a live Run only (after a teardown began a result only adds its receipt); only an indeterminate result keeps a receipt for reconcile:.
limits: One node: the host fences the processes of its own Runs by their group leader (a process that changes its own group leader escapes it) and no Store write; every predecessor check rests on the caller's fencing_proof, which this Piece cannot check. Two hosts in one VM stand for two nodes in the tests; one host per node is not enforced, and two hosts in one VM need distinct names.

Store Need: every write of every view is a compare-and-set on its stream head (the integration/sql PostgreSQL and the Memory Stores are) and every EffectIntent send follows its committed arm. A write that a predecessor submitted can still commit after the host's own confirmed teardown; whether one can is what fencing_proof attests, and the host claims nothing about outstanding writes beyond that attestation.

Profile: protocol version 1, no expiry_reports or messages option, no local work, Resource, outside event, tool call or other Effect binding, so no asynchronous engine input bypasses the host and the deadlines, Attempt and terminal phase are read only at the refresh points. ASK model calls wait until the Run ends.

Routes are read from the whole retained transcript (at most 65,536 records and 536,870,912 bytes). Sink deliveries are volatile: a delivery lost with the worker leaves its slot open, and no reconciliation of intents is supplied; the intent's durable settlement can differ from the engine's slot. A provider request already on the wire is not recalled by a teardown.

A host input that the engine answers {:error, :unavailable} or an exit is sent again under the same ID, frame and context at most 20 times (200 ms times the attempt), then reported; another refusal is reported. A trusted context that gives no future pause deadline is outside the engine's Need: an outcome is reported and not submitted, a wake is tried again a second later.

Renewal and expiry are timed on the node's monotonic clock from lease-clock samples, sound for a lease clock that runs no slower than the node's: at the Run's deadline the Run is lost with no reading, and a slower lease clock gets more time only from the expiry check's reading min(200 ms, TTL/4) before it; admission and activation also read the lease clock. A renewal that waits the whole 5,000 ms caller limit ends before the deadline only for a TTL of 10 s or more; with a smaller TTL, a renewal whose reply comes after the deadline, or one whose lease cannot be read after its reply before it, the Run stops (on_lost :expired). A lease record is identified by its sequence (Lease.status/2 and Lease.retention_bound/2 at one head revision, five tries), not its until; every live reading (renewal, expiry check, admission, activation) is ordered by head revision, lease clock sample, then node time. Once a newer reading shows another lease record of this owner (a re-claim), the host starts no renewal of it and the Run is fenced at its deadline; a renewal already submitted is not recalled and can append onto the re-claim's record before the owner reports :fenced. {:error, :lease_lost} is admission, not a physical fence: an input already with the worker can reach the engine until the teardown stops it.

A per-Run keep-alive touches the Unit through the directory every quarter of idle_ms from each engine start, input or control until a status read shows no model call ready or running; a directory busy for longer than three quarters of idle_ms can still let the Unit sleep under a call. An engine call that ends only by its 60 s call limit holds the worker that long. The wake timer waits the difference of the engine clock's milliseconds on the node's timers: a Run deadline is reached on time only with an engine clock that runs in real time.

Reports are Logger warnings with the Run reference and the action, key or input ID, never a payload; no telemetry event. A callback that calls reap/2 for its own Run is stopped by that reap and gets no reply.

Finite disposable-PostgreSQL scenarios with Memory scenarios and the scripted Req stub of integration/ai-text-anthropic: no live provider, no production fencing, cluster ownership or exactly-once external effect is shown.

grounding.claim: The groups end_to_end, model_call_not_completed, capacity, callbacks and options_and_profile: an AgentLoop Run started with start_run/3 and its typed start through input/5 answers with the scripted stub, result/4 returns the completed record before reap/2 and {:error, :not_running} after it, on disposable PostgreSQL and on one Memory namespace whose fold restores a sleeping Unit (status and result read again after the Unit slept), with one manual-clock Lease backend and allow_volatile; a model call answered 500 ends the Run failed with no host cancel; with max_runs 2 held by a terminal Run and a Run whose Unit sleeps, a third start is {:error, :capacity}, and after reap/2 none of the Run's processes is alive (found without the host's tracking and collected in the test process: spawn tracing set on the host for the start and on the host's shared task supervisor, whose Run tasks include the held on_terminal callback, at least 13 processes with the worker, the engine and that callback among them, and the Unit with its Writer from the directory's Registry), the lease is free and a start is admitted; a reap whose lease release fails is {:error, :release_unconfirmed} with the slot kept until a later reap; a start and a wake waiting on an unconfirmed release are answered with no third request (the start takes the key over, its proof holding the torn-down tenure's Unit and Writer); a failed start whose release fails twice keeps its slot until the release is confirmed; a reap that joins a failed start's release that fails is {:error, :release_unconfirmed}, the release is still tried until confirmed and a start then succeeds with no other call; a wake that waits on a release that fails and whose spec callback fails before its claim is {:spec, :unknown_run}, and the old lease is still released, so another owner claims it; with max_runs 2, while a wake's tenure owes an old lease's release and its spec callback is held, a start of another Run of that Unit is {:error, :identity_in_use}, and once the callback fails ({:spec, :gone}) the old lease is released, no Run is left and another owner claims the key; an unconfirmed release result delivered under the release job's reference while its task still runs frees nothing and hands nothing over (the reap and a waiting start unanswered for 300 ms, the same tenure releasing), and once the task has exited the reap is {:error, :release_unconfirmed} and the start takes the key over as a new tenure; the same holds when a callback :DOWN of the tenure reaches the host after that result and before the task's exit (a monitor entry put into the host's state by the test: a deterministic mailbox ordering, not a reproduced race); a blocked on_terminal is stopped by reap before the slot is freed and a callback that reaps its own Run does not deadlock; option, profile and unit-bound refusals; Units x and run/x keep six distinct streams and both complete; a killed Registry stops the host with :killed; a host with no name takes the Registry names of its owner_id, the same after a restart, and a second host on them is refused {:already_started, _}; a Run's group leader is gone after its reap and after a normal stop of its host; a killed host's link ends the Run's worker with the host's own exit reason :killed, and every process of the Run then ends.

The groups admission_refusal, sink_route, unit_awake, route_verification and translation: an image part is a gate denial unsupported_feature settled refused with no intent stream, no activation record and no stub request; the intent key is ai-text's key of the SHA-256 of {run_id, attempt_id, action_id}, the input ID is 67 bytes from Run, Attempt and occurrence, and a duplicate sink delivery (traced) gives no second engine input; under budget_rule :pause the duplicate keeps the first pause deadline after the context changed; with retention 1 a delivery after Unit dedup eviction adds no journal input, and a retry due after a successful duplicate submits nothing (two engine calls in all); a transport timeout commits dispatch unknown with no actual; a 70 KiB completion, and a small one whose tool arguments reach 32 levels with a reported usage that converts, each commit refused too_large dispatched with no actual (each with its reservation of 1,000 still reserved and nothing committed), and the same completion one level shallower commits completed with actual 2,598; a sink_failed delivery gives no input and the slot stays running; an outcome survives a failed route read and settles once; a successful call held past idle_ms of 300 ms settles completed; after a begin_attempt in the middle of a Run the old-Attempt delivery reaches the engine under its own Attempt with no route report, the new call settles completed and each settles once, with intent keys of their own Attempts; with idle_ms 300 and the adapter's model catalog unloaded, a first model call whose input waits for the catalog load settles completed with no warm-up; a transcript read that holds the worker 1.5 s with a call in flight leaves the same Unit live and the call settles completed; an idle Run's Unit sleeps; each wake of route_verification passes a proof whose list holds the reaped first tenure's traced processes and its Unit and Writer from the directory's Registry, all ended; a wake whose route read gives history at once, or after an unavailable read, is {:route, :history} and leaves no Run; a live delivery whose route cannot be read is reported with no input; a sink failure held during a wake's route verification is reported once the route is read and the worker stays live; every ai-text outcome has its input form.

The groups crash_and_wake, routing, teardown, fingerprint_and_dispositions and lease_fencing, each proof that lets a check pass demonstrated by the test (the predecessor's processes, found by spawn tracing or the stand-in node's group-leader chains within four hops and collected in the test process, hold one that the test saw itself and, where the predecessor started an engine, its Unit and that Unit's Writer from the directory's Registry, taken before the teardown (a predecessor that started no engine is traced to have started no Unit), and have ended; a held write has landed; only the test of the proof asked at each check scripts its answers): with the stub blocked inside the call, a same-node restart after the host's own teardown is fencing_unproven with no engine start until the proof is given, and a host on another stand-in node frozen past its lease is taken over by a second host whose fencing_proof observes that every process of that node has ended (its list: every process whose group-leader chain reaches the node's leader within four group-leader hops when the list is taken (a snapshot of those chains, not an unbounded traversal), asserted to hold the host and the node's Unit and Writer from its directory's Registry; refused while they live; the test calls fence_node outside the proof); in each the stub is called once, the slot settles unknown once with lost_outcome and the Run reads failed with model_call_not_completed; lease expiry alone with no fencing_proof is fencing_unproven with no engine start (traced), no activation record and no new send, at a second wake too; on Memory, an EffectIntent settlement append held after its submission across the host's own confirmed teardown gives fencing_unproven with no engine, activation or send while held, then lands on the unchanged intent head, and a wake with proof reads it (the recovered owner at that revision) and the slot settles lost_outcome once; a start_run/3 retry on an existing journal, and a fresh start whose worker is killed after its create, are fencing_unproven with no engine until a proof, then start with create and begin_attempt duplicate and one Attempt; the proof is asked at each check; a lease seized during an engine input denies the activation (no activation record, no stub request) and loses the Run once; on Memory, an activation on this owner's lease that a re-claim shortened to 1 s, with the lease clock 2 s on, is denied with no activation record and no stub request and loses the Run :expired once; an intent admitted and never armed is recovered at wake, sent once, its outcome held in the worker until the route is verified, with three activation records and one settlement each; a wake whose engine start dispatches such an intent (its proof answering :fenced before the wake, the first tenure's Unit and Writer included) while its first route read is held 1.5 s past an idle_ms of 300 ms keeps the same Unit live and the call settles completed with one stub request; a buffered completion that ends the Run after a route read that failed once is answered :woken and calls on_terminal once; a read-only intent owner whose activation head read failed, and a send task that traps exits after its task supervisor died, are stopped; a changed gate version or request cap is fencing_unproven without a proof and incompatible_recovery with one, the Unit stopped while the batch wakes another Run; a batch whose dispositions are all immediate is answered once, and a batch with a live Run, a Run with no current Attempt and one whose lease another owner holds gives one disposition each with no engine start and leaves none of its processes alive; a second host's start or wake on a held key is the lease refusal with no engine start on PostgreSQL and, with one shared Lease backend, on Memory.

The groups deadlines, call_limit, lease_clock and renewal: an idle Run ends out_of_time by the host's wake at its deadline; a paused Run ends at the earlier deadline in both orderings (a pause control whose pause deadline is after the Run deadline, and a Budget exhaustion under budget_rule :pause whose pause deadline comes first), each wake under the digest ID of that deadline; a continue that replaces the Run deadline moves the timer and the old deadline gives no wake; a wake held in the engine past its pause operand is refused and sent again with a fresh one; a refused wake is sent again only by its timer, at least 950 ms later, under the new Attempt after a begin_attempt; engine reads that end by the 60 s call limit decide nothing: no wake until the deadline is read, an input queued behind a begin_attempt is forwarded only after the new Attempt is read, its call keyed and routed under it, a control and an input queued behind a cancel whose read after it ended by the call limit are each {:error, :terminal} with no engine call (traced), on_terminal is called once and the terminal observation stays confirmed, and an input, and separately a control, queued behind a sink completion that ends the Run, whose read after that input ended by the call limit, are each {:error, :terminal} with no engine call (traced) and on_terminal is called once; a Memory lease clock moved 61 s past a 60 s TTL stops admission (on_lost :expired); a claim held 2.5 s before its lease sample with a TTL of 2 s keeps its lease and the Run completes; a caller held between its admission and its lease reading while a renewal is confirmed is admitted again with no loss; on PostgreSQL a Run lives through three TTLs of 1,000 ms (six different messages 500 ms apart, each applied) with at least four committed renewals and four host-confirmed generations, then completes with no loss; a step not applied fails with the reply, process exits, callbacks, the host's lease state and the renewal count, and no Store data; a seized lease is lost (on_lost lease_lost), admission stops and every process of the Run ends; time is measured on both sides of a loss, against a cutoff that the test measures itself (its own store-clock reading, a re-claim's own sample, or the node times around a start on a lease clock that it does not move) less a 250 ms sampling margin and plus a 300 ms timer margin, only for the renewal whose reply would come after the deadline, the two Runs whose Memory readings are blocked and the renewal whose lease a re-claim shortened; the first-reading-fails renewal, the seized-before-reading renewal and the two shortened-lease orderings are bounded by a test-controlled event and a measured upper bound; every other loss is checked by reason, receipt and order with no clock measurement; a renewal that commits but whose reply would come 1.5 s later, past the last confirmed until, is on_lost :expired once at the claim's until and before that reply; on Memory, a renewal that sampled the lease clock 2 s into a 4 s TTL, whose reply comes after the clock passed the last confirmed until and whose first reading after it fails, is read again, both readings in reader tasks that the renewal task started, and is on_lost :expired once after the test lets the task go on and before the host's deadline could come; a renewal that commits and whose lease an operator seizes before its reading is on_lost {:lease_lost, holder operator} once, with no input, after the seizure and before the claim's until; a renewal whose reply is held 6 s, past the 5 s caller limit, is on_lost {:unknown, :no_receipt}, the host stays alive with admission stopped, the old owner is gone before the wake that replaces it, the late renewal committed, and no receipt is kept; an indeterminate renewal result that reaches the host before the owner's exit is on_lost once with that receipt, given as reconcile: to the next start, and the Run completes; an indeterminate renewal whose result comes after the teardown keeps the Run's slot until that job ends, is on_lost once, and its receipt is kept and reconciled at the next start; a worker's report of an indeterminate owner exit that reaches the host first is on_lost once, stops admission and keeps the receipt; a reap during a renewal gives no on_lost and frees the lease; a reap waits for a held renewal job, also after a result reached the host while the job's process ran, until that process exits, before it frees the slot; a renewal's unconfirmed result that reaches the host while its task still runs, with a reap right behind it, is on_lost at once with admission stopped, and that reap still waits for the task's exit; on Memory, with the lease readings blocked at the deadline (the backend suspended right after a renewal's reply, or held inside a renewal), each Run is on_lost :expired at its deadline (2 s after its start, the lease clock still) and its teardown ends within 2 s, while the readings still wait in the backend; a renewal whose lease a same-holder re-claim shortened to 1 s before its reading is on_lost :expired at the re-claim's until, with no input and no renewal of the re-claim's record; on Memory, a renewal's reading after its reply, a same-holder re-claim to 1 s and an expiry check's reading, read by the backend in that order, with the renewal's confirmation applied after the check's newer reading and, separately, before it (the other job held), each leave the renewal's until confirmed and the re-claim's shorter deadline, and the Run is on_lost :expired by that deadline plus 300 ms with no renewal of the re-claim's record; a renewal whose reading after its reply is given up at a deadline that an expiry reading has since moved later (the lease clock behind the node's) is confirmed by a reading that the host takes after its reply, the Run not lost by the moved deadline plus 300 ms and renewed again; a lease reader that replied and is suspended before its exit gives its reading at once (under 1 s, its deadline 5 s away), is killed and its exit awaited, and the reading spawns no process (traced); on Memory, each ordering fixed by the test: a same-holder re-claim with the same until as the renewal, committed before the renewal's reading, shows another lease record, and no renewal starts past the next renewal's moment; an expiry check reading the confirmation's head revision, lease time and record later on the node moves the deadline, so a renewal held in the owner past the old deadline is confirmed with no loss; a shorter same-holder re-claim read by a caller's admission and, separately, by a granted EffectIntent activation moves the deadline to the re-claim's and starts no renewal; a not-yet-started renewal whose deadline a newer reading of the confirmed record shortens starts at once, once, and is confirmed with no loss; on PostgreSQL, a renewal held in the owner before its lock while the host observes a same-holder re-claim then appends a renewal onto the re-claim's record (its until extended) and the owner answers :fenced with that record's revision, on_lost once and no other renewal started.

Pinned GenServer, Registry, DynamicSupervisor, Task.Supervisor and Process link, monitor, group leader and timer semantics carry the host, its workers, the teardown and the timers; no local OTP runtime proof.
OTP 29.1.3 exit signals (an untrappable kill), links, monitors, group-leader inheritance at spawn (each Run's process set and the tests' stand-in node) and ETF/SHA-256 for the derived identities.

The caller supplies compatible Store views of one namespace whose writes are compare-and-set on their stream heads, a Lease over the Run view, trusted callbacks (a spec rebuilt from durable facts with stable identities, a context that gives a future pause deadline when sampled, a prompt clock in real time) and a fencing_proof that answers :fenced only when no predecessor process can still act and no Store write that a predecessor submitted can still commit, on this node or another; it supervises the host, gives each Run one stable run_ref and Unit identity, keeps full retained history, and runs no code that changes a Run process's group leader. Scripted stubs and local PostgreSQL do not establish production fencing or provider behaviour.

telemetry.contract: OTP diagnostics and a Logger warning (Run reference and action, key or input ID, no payload) for a delivery that gives the engine no input: a sink failure, no route, a route that cannot be read, no future pause deadline, a refused or untaken input; no custom event or exporter.

config.contract: Fixed construction options (owner_id, max_runs, idle_ms, the five Store views, Lease, clock, lease_ttl_ms, spec callback; optional fencing_proof, on_terminal, on_lost, allow_volatile, name) refused as invalid_options when missing, malformed, out of range or of mixed namespaces; per-Run specs checked at start; no hot change.

control.contract: start_run/3, wake/2 (one disposition per Run), reap/2 with confirmed teardown and confirmed release (else release_unconfirmed), and pass-through input/5 and control/5 with :not_running, :terminal, :lease_lost and :unavailable admission and no Approval control; renewal, expiry checks and deadline wakes are the host's own.
